reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. While both plans prioritize easy running, Plan A incorporates more frequent runs focused on building confidence and reinforcing trail-running fundamentals, which is crucial for developing the mental and physical resilience needed for faster times. Furthermore, Plan A includes a run with a slight incline, directly addressing hill strength, a key component of trail running performance. Plan B’s emphasis on purely easy runs and a strength session feels less targeted towards improving speed and more focused on general fitness, neglecting the specific demands of trail running.
